points.text: M1: acyl chlorides > alkyl chlorides > aryl chlorides; fastest to slowest

acyl chlorides carbon in $\text{C–Cl}$ bond is more electron deficient since it is also attached to an oxygen atom OR $\text{C–Cl}$ bond is weakest / weakened in acyl chlorides since it is also attached to an oxygen atom / two electronegative atoms

aryl chlorides (no hydrolysis) $\text{C–Cl}$ bond is part of delocalised system / partially double bond character (so $\text{C–Cl}$ bond is stronger) OR lone pair / p-orbital on $\text{Cl}$ delocalises with $\pi$ ring (so $\text{C–Cl}$ bond is stronger)

alkyl chlorides $\text{C–Cl}$ bond strengthened by electron donating effect / positive inductive effect of alkyl / R group (as compared to acyl chlorides) OR carbon atom has a smaller $\delta+$ and the $\text{C–Cl}$ bond is stronger (than the $\text{C–Cl}$ bond in $\text{COCl}$) due to (the carbon) being only attached to one electronegative atom

4-(phenylimino-substituted) piperidine propanoic acid derivative: $\text{HO-C(=O)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-N(piperidin-1-yl)-C(COOH)(NHPh)}$ at 4-position, i.e. piperidine with $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{C(=O)OH}$ on N and $\text{C(COOH)(NHPh)}$ with phenyl ring via NH at C-4
